title: Chicken Roasted With Curry, Grapefruit, Honey and Thyme
description: By Colu Henry: Sweet and savory curry powder is combined with honey and a pleasantly tart grapefruit juice to create a rich glaze for your above-average weeknight bird. Roasting the chicken low and slow keeps the meat moist, and basting frequently prevents the caramelization of the sauce from scorching. Serve with a side of greens such as spinach, kale or Swiss chard that have been sautéed in lots of garlic and oil.
ingredients: ⅓ cup grapefruit juice, freshly squeezed, if possible
Sprinkle of red pepper flakes (or a little spice [like cayenne] to taste, or use some hot honey above)
1 tablespoon finely chopped thyme, fresh preferably, but dried OK
Fingerling potatoes, carrots, shallots, peeled garlic cloves, etc (optional)
Some oil or a little butter
directions: Pat the chicken dry and season it well with salt and pepper, both inside and out. Place the chicken breast-side up in a 10-inch ovenproof skillet or roasting pan. Add some water or broth, maybe with a little butter or oil, to keep everything moist.
In a medium bowl, whisk together the grapefruit juice, honey, spices, curry powder and thyme. Spoon all the mixture over the chicken, making sure it is evenly covered.
Roast the chicken for 30 minutes, basting every 15 minutes or so.

Turn heat down to 325 degrees and continue basting the chicken with the pan juices until the skin is lacquered with sauce and the chicken registers 165 degrees with an instant thermometer in the thickest part of the thigh, about 45 to 50 minutes more.
Add some potatoes or other little sides for roasting in the last 30 minutes or so.
If chicken skin is starting to become too dark, tent with foil.
Allow the chicken to rest (maybe upside down) for 10 minutes before carving.
